name: Topiramate
summary: A broad-spectrum anticonvulsant with multiple mechanisms that also prevents migraine and causes weight loss, at the cost of cognitive and renal side effects.
mechanism: Multiple actions: use-dependent sodium channel block, GABA-A potentiation, AMPA/kainate glutamate antagonism, and weak carbonic anhydrase inhibition.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Partial hepatic metabolism (hydroxylation, hydrolysis, glucuronidation); ~70% excreted unchanged in urine

dosing.adult: Start 25 mg/day, titrate weekly; usual maintenance 100–200 mg BID (epilepsy) or 50–100 mg BID (migraine prophylaxis)
dosing.renalAdjustment: Halve the dose when CrCl <70 mL/min

safety.pregnancy: Teratogenic — increased risk of oral clefts; avoid in pregnancy and counsel women of childbearing age
warnings: Acute angle-closure glaucoma (rare, idiosyncratic) — urgent if eye pain or sudden vision loss
Nephrolithiasis and hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis from carbonic anhydrase inhibition
Teratogenic — oral cleft risk; pregnancy prevention counseling needed
Cognitive impairment — word-finding difficulty and concentration problems (dose-limiting)
Hyperammonemia with or without encephalopathy when combined with valproate
safety.overdose: Metabolic acidosis, seizures, CNS depression; supportive care

clinicalPearls: Weight loss plus migraine prophylaxis in one drug — attractive in migraineurs with obesity
Carbonic anhydrase inhibition explains both kidney stones and metabolic acidosis — counsel hydration
good: Epilepsy complicated by migraine or obesity — two birds with one stone.
bad: Patients needing sharp cognition, or those with kidney stones or acidosis risk.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard neurology/pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
